content.text: {"answer":"These results don’t directly address how to use a more detailed understanding of user goals to improve recommender systems. However, one paper connected to recommender goals and user experience studies when fairness-driven novelty/exploration should be reduced for individuals, showing that “uniform fairness or novelty pressure can disproportionately disadvantage certain users” due to user-dependent exploration saturation [8].\n\nPaper [8] defines exploration saturation as the point where further increases in exploration no longer improve user utility and may reduce engagement or perceived relevance, and it finds that users with limited interaction histories reach saturation earlier. In contrast, the other fairness papers focus on formal fairness trade-offs, thresholding under constraints, fairness verification, or fairness evaluation/tooling rather than modeling user goals within recommendation policies [1-7,9-10].","grounded":false}
